task.text: Support renames a user, reloads the page, and still sees the old name.

`UserService` is a cache-aside layer over a `UserStore` (given): read the cache first, fall back to the store on a miss, and keep the store as the source of truth. It has two bugs. Fix them without changing any signature.

items: After `rename(id, name)` the next `get(id)` must return the new name. Write the store first, then evict that one entry.
A user that does not exist yet must not be remembered as absent: once it is created, `get` finds it.
The TTL and the injected clock stay as they are.

checks.title: A second read is served from the cache
A rename shows up on the next read
A rename evicts only its own entry

hints.text: Two different bugs, one cause: the cache is trusted more than the store. One is about what happens *after a write*, the other about what a *miss* is allowed to store.
In `rename`, after `store.save`, remove only that key from `cache`. In `get`, put an entry only when the store returned a row; an empty `Optional` must leave the cache untouched.
